title: Repository error messages are hard to understand

labels.name: P1
labels.description: I'll work on this now. (Assignee required)

labels.name: team-ExternalDeps
labels.description: External dependency handling, remote repositiories, WORKSPACE file.

labels.name: bad error messaging
labels.description: Issues where users get stuck because they don't understand what they did wrong

body:
ERROR: .../envoy/bazel/repositories.bzl:534:5: no such package '@com_google_protobuf_cc//': java.io.IOException: Error downloading [https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/archive/7492b5681231c79f0265793fa57dc780ae2481d6.tar.gz] to .../ced7d3877a6bbc9c6bf06f67d3a47b5b/external/com_google_protobuf_cc/7492b5681231c79f0265793fa57dc780ae2481d6.tar.gz: Unknown host: github.com and referenced by '//external:protoc'

This error message has proved difficult to parse for people who aren't intimately familiar with bazel's internals. It's a series of stacked exceptions and causes, which leads users in the wrong direction.

The initial line number reference is to https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/414f56f6b3ed5d99f3c23ee3bfee71c1905edeea/bazel/repositories.bzl#L534 which is the place where com_google_protobuf_cc is used.

Initially, you have to understand the relatively obscure native.bind construct to see that this is just a use site. Then you have to determine which parts of the exception are really about the definition of this repository, and then you have to go hunt down where that repository is really defined, which the error doesn't tell you about at all.

The "and referenced by '//external:protoc'" part on the end is a complete distraction which doesn't help at all.

What I would like to have seen here is:

ERROR: .../envoy/bazel/repositories.bzl:518:5: Error downloading [https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/archive/7492b5681231c79f0265793fa57dc780ae2481d6.tar.gz] to .../ced7d3877a6bbc9c6bf06f67d3a47b5b/external/com_google_protobuf_cc/7492b5681231c79f0265793fa57dc780ae2481d6.tar.gz: Unknown host: github.com
.../envoy/bazel/repositories.bzl:534:5: @com_google_protobuf_cc referenced from here

The situation is worse when there is a chain of dependencies involved (where needing to fetch one repo led to needing to download another, which fails) as it will accumulate errors from each of them in turn, and the user must track down exactly what happened. The exception which is the cause of the problem will be buried somewhere in the middle of a stack of messages which are really just trying to be a list of references.

For maximum confusion, if the underlying error was caused by a repository_ctx.execute step failing, then the real error (the output of the failed command) will be printed on a few lines above all this, with no clear framing to indicate what it was the output of. It would be much better if this was handled like failed build steps, so the repository which could not be be fetched printed an error like "output from failed command follows: [...]"
